description: Standalone route (/accept-invite?token=...) rendering a form to set a name and password and accept a team invite via AuthContext.acceptInvite, then redirects to the dashboard. Wraps the form in a Suspense boundary because it reads the invite token from useSearchParams.
Binary favicon icon asset (~26KB .ico) served by Next.js as the site's browser tab icon.

Global Tailwind v4 stylesheet: imports Tailwind, defines the app's light/dark CSS custom properties (the 'Aqua Bloom' color palette), a custom dark-mode variant tied to a manual .dark class, the app-shell viewport-height fix, keyframe animations (fade/scale/gradient/shimmer), the animated Aqua sky/tree/petal background scene and its dark-mode Night scene counterpart, skeleton loader styling, and scrollbar/selection/focus styling.

Root Next.js layout: loads Sora/Inter/JetBrains Mono Google fonts as CSS variables, sets page metadata/viewport, links the Phosphor icon web font stylesheets, and wraps all page content in the Providers and ThemeProvider context trees.

The single top-level dashboard route. Holds the active top-nav tab ('Dashboard' | 'Tests' | 'Scan Results' | 'Automation' | 'Settings') in local state and renders the matching screen (DashboardHub, TestManagementPage, ScanResultsPage, AutomationPage, SettingsPage) inside the shared Layout shell.
Composes the app's global React context providers in dependency order: AuthProvider > ToastProvider > QADataProvider > ReportModalProvider > NewTestModalProvider, wrapping all page children.

Standalone shareable ticket page for a single issue, addressed by testId+issueId. Builds the issue row from QADataContext via buildIssueRows, shows severity/phase/screenshot, a resolution code-fix blueprint (from a real applied PR fix, a located source file, or a generic template), assignee management, comments, and re-test/resolve actions — mirrors the ticket detail shown inline in IssuesPage but as its own URL.
Shared prop/data-shape TypeScript interfaces for dashboard-area UI: StatCardProps, PipelineStep/TestPipelineData, and IssueItem (used by StatCard, TestPipeline, and UnresolvedIssues).
Defines the TestRun interface, a lightweight/legacy shape describing a single test run (id, targetUrl, testType, status, issues, score, date).

Fetches an annotated (or full-page) screenshot for a given testId+issueId from /ai-automation/annotated-screenshot and displays it alongside the CSS selector and page path of the affected component, with loading and 'unavailable' states.

Dashboard widget that scans a given URL via POST /api/generate-playwright-code to auto-generate a section-grouped manual QA test-case matrix (with screenshots), previews it as tables, and lets the user export the result as a printable PDF or a Word (.doc) document with embedded (base64) screenshots.

Displays a CI/CD-style automated check summary (total/passed/failed/skipped counts, pass rate, status badge) for the AI Automation pipeline, with a togglable raw pipeline-log viewer and a link to the GitHub Actions run when available.

Standalone AI code-review tool: lets the user paste a code snippet, pick a language, and POST it to /ai-automation/review-code; renders the returned summary, per-line severity-tagged issues, and a corrected-code block with copy-to-clipboard.
Presentational card showing an AI-classified issue's type/category/severity badges plus its root cause and suggested fix text, used within the AI Automation pipeline results view.

Shows the details of an AI-generated pull request (target repo/branch, PR title, status, matched-by info), a link to view it on GitHub, and an optional in-app approval-gate 'Check Approval & Merge' action with loading/error/merged states.
Renders AI-generated release notes for a resolved (or pending) issue: fixed/pending badge, affected component, and impact/notes text.

Lets the user trigger a real re-scan/re-check of a specific issue via POST /ai-automation/verify and displays whether it's now resolved, partially resolved, or still failing, with supporting evidence text; explains when verification isn't supported for a given issue category.
Top-of-page summary card for the AI Automation pipeline showing the bug ticket ID/title/severity, an AI confidence score gauge (via ScoreGauge), and the scan date.

Gradient hero banner on the dashboard overview showing the signed-in user's greeting, overall average QA score, a dynamic health message derived from score/critical-issue count, and quick stat chips (tests run, issues found, critical count) pulled from QADataContext.

Renders the realistic device chrome (status bar, browser bar, notch/home-indicator or desktop titlebar) around a live screenshot frame streamed from the Device Lab session, translating clicks/scroll/keyboard events on the frame into normalized device-viewport coordinates and forwarding them via passed-in handlers; also draws the DevTools 'inspect element' highlight box.

A Chrome-DevTools-style panel with Elements/Console/Network/Sources/Performance/Memory/Application tabs for the live Device Lab session — shows console logs, network requests, a DOM tree with box-model/styles pane for inspected elements, per-file source viewing, and performance/memory/storage snapshots pulled from useDeviceLabSession.

Parses an HTML string with DOMParser and renders it as a collapsible, syntax-highlighted DOM tree (like DevTools' Elements panel), supporting expand/collapse per node and syncing selection/expansion to an externally-selected CSS selector (e.g. from the on-device element picker).

The app's persistent shell: renders the sidebar nav (Dashboard/Tests/Scan Results/Automation/Settings tabs), the animated Aqua/Night background scenes, the top header with search input, ThemeToggle, and an account popup that switches between sign-in, forgot-password, and register forms (wired to AuthContext) or a signed-in session panel; also handles mobile off-canvas nav.

Renders whichever Phase 2 QA module results exist on a completed test (accessibility violations, SEO checks, visual regression via VisualRegressionPanel, cross-browser results, performance benchmark deltas), returning null entirely if none ran.

Modal (driven by ReportModalContext's activeTestId) showing a single test's full report: live progress bar while running/queued, a launch animation on pass/fail, Lighthouse score gauges and policy grading, responsive screenshots, Phase2ResultsPanel, and a resolve/reopen-capable issues list, with a re-run action.

Renders a grid of Recharts visualizations built from real completed-test data in QADataContext: QA score per site (bar), issues by severity (donut), score trend over time (area), average Lighthouse category scores (bar), pass/fail split (donut), and issues by category (bar); shows an empty state until at least one scan completes.

Table of all completed (passed/failed) tests with per-row Lighthouse mini-scores, broken-link count, overall score, completion date, and an 'Inspect' button that opens the ReportDetailModal for that test.

A framer-motion celebratory/informational animation (cloud puffs + a rocket flying through, then settling into a Pass/Fail label) shown briefly (5s) whenever a scan's result first renders in the report modal or Phase 2 results page.
Four-card KPI strip (Total Tests, Average Quality Score, Resolved Issues, Failed Scans) computed from QADataContext's stats/tests, with skeleton loading placeholders and animated counters.

Two-panel widget: a left area-chart toggling between mock 'quality'/'coverage' trend series (dynamically dated but not backed by real per-day data), and a right severity-distribution breakdown of real unresolved issue counts from QADataContext stats, with progress bars per severity.

Displays per-viewport visual-regression results (perfect/good/bad/new-baseline verdict badges) with a side-by-side baseline-vs-current image toggle and a diff-highlight image view, pulling image URLs through api.screenshotUrl.

Generic animated stat tile used across dashboard/team/analytics screens: renders a title, an animated numeric counter (via AnimatedCounter), optional sub-value text, and a colored icon badge whose gradient depends on the 'variant' prop (primary/warning/danger/success).

Status filter tab group (All/Completed/Running/Failed) plus a sort-order dropdown (newest/oldest/score desc/asc) for the Test Management table; labels come from useContent so they're editable via content.json.
Header bar for the Test Management screen: page title/subtitle, a search input, and a 'Run New Test' button that opens the NewTestModal.

Modal form for starting a new scan: URL input, Phase 1 (always-on) vs Phase 2 (opt-in checkboxes from PHASE2_MODULES) module selection, an optional testing-policy dropdown fetched from api.policies.list, and submits via the onStartTest callback; fires onExited once its framer-motion exit animation truly completes.

Paginated table of tests (URL, pages scanned, status badge, critical-issue count, score, date, and view/rerun/delete actions), with skeleton rows while loading and an EmptyState when there are no tests.

Visualizes the currently-running (or latest) test's pipeline stage progress as a horizontal step tracker (Crawl/Responsive/Performance/Console/Links), with a status pill and a 'View Full Report' button that opens ReportModalContext for that test.
Header icon button that toggles between light/dark theme on left-click, and opens a small light/dark/system dropdown menu on right-click, driven by ThemeContext.
Thin wrapper around the useCountUp hook that renders an animated, easing count-up to a target numeric value.

Purely decorative, non-interactive light-mode background: SVG clouds drifting, trees swaying, and falling petals, absolutely positioned and hidden in dark mode / under prefers-reduced-motion via CSS classes defined in globals.css.
Generic centered empty-state placeholder (icon, title, optional description and action node) reused across tables/lists when there is no data.
Dark-mode counterpart to AquaScene: a glowing moon, twinkling stars, sparkles, drifting clouds, and a shooting star, shown only when the .dark class is active (controlled via CSS in globals.css).

Circular SVG progress gauge that animates from 0 to a given 0-100 score, color-coded by score band (green/blue/amber/red), used for Lighthouse category scores and AI confidence scores throughout the app.
Minimal shimmering placeholder block (relies on the .skeleton CSS animation in globals.css) used for loading states across tables and cards.
Dashboard widget listing the top unresolved issue categories (label + count, color-coded by severity), passed in as an `issues` prop; shows an empty-state message when there are none.

Authentication context: persists a JWT + user object to localStorage or sessionStorage (based on 'remember me'), validates the saved session against /api/auth/me on mount, and exposes login/register/forgotPassword/acceptInvite/logout methods that call the backend auth endpoints directly via fetch.

Provides the useContent(key, defaults) hook that looks up a labeled block (text/icon/imageUrl) from the static lib/content.json editorial-content file, falling back to caller-supplied defaults — used to make UI copy/icons/images swappable without code changes.

Manages the global 'Run New Test' modal's open/close state and mounts the NewTestModal once at the provider level; on successful test creation it shows a toast and, once the modal's exit animation truly finishes (via onExited), opens the ReportDetailModal for the new test.

Central data store for tests/stats/pipeline: fetches all three from the backend API on mount and polls every 3s while any scan is active (else 12s), and exposes createTest/rerunTest/deleteTest/updateIssue/assignIssue/addIssueComment mutators that call the API then refetch everything.
Tracks which test's report modal (if any) is currently open (by testId) and mounts a single shared ReportDetailModal instance at the provider level.

Manages light/dark/system theme preference, persisting the choice to localStorage, resolving 'system' against the OS prefers-color-scheme media query, and toggling the .light/.dark class on <html> so Tailwind's dark: variant and globals.css theme variables respond.
Provides a showToast(message, type) function and renders a stack of auto-dismissing (3.5s) animated toast notifications (success/error/info) fixed to the bottom-right of the screen.
requestAnimationFrame-driven hook that eases a displayed number from its previous value up to a new `target` over `duration` ms (cubic ease-out), used by AnimatedCounter.

Owns a socket.io connection to the backend's /device-lab namespace for a live Playwright-driven device session: starts/reconnects sessions, streams screenshot frames, console logs, network requests, DOM HTML, element-inspection results, storage/cookies, performance metrics, memory info, and per-file source, and exposes input-forwarding functions (click/scroll/type/navigate) plus inspect/fetch actions.
Generic setInterval-based polling hook that repeatedly invokes a (ref-stabilized) callback every intervalMs while `enabled` is true, cleaning up the interval on unmount or disable.
Fetches a single test by id via api.getTest, exposing test/loading/error/refetch, and auto-polls every 2.5s while that test is queued or running (via usePolling).

Defines the IssueRow shape (a flattened, ticket-oriented view of a backend issue) and buildIssueRows(tests), which flattens every test's issues into a single sorted (newest-first) array with a generated ticket/report ID, category label, and the test's first available screenshot as a visual reference.

Central typed HTTP client for the Express backend: reads the JWT from the same 'qa_auth' storage key AuthContext writes, wraps fetch with auth-header injection and unreachable-backend/error-message handling, and exposes the `api` object grouping every endpoint (tests, issues, stats, pipeline, policies, branding, team, monitors, analytics, device lab) plus API_BASE_URL/API_ORIGIN constants and device-lab type definitions.
Small (73-line) JSON data file of keyed editorial content blocks (text/icon/imageUrl) consumed by ContentContext's useContent hook to make UI copy/labels swappable without code edits.

Report/document export utilities: fetches white-label branding (logo/colors/header/footer) with a safe fallback, builds jsPDF and docx (Word) documents and CSV text for both a full scan report and a scoped ticket list, embedding the branding logo and rendering Lighthouse scores, accessibility/SEO/visual-regression/cross-browser/performance sections, and the issues table; also triggers the browser download.

getDynamicFixCode(title): a large keyword-matching function that returns a hardcoded example code snippet (performance/accessibility/SEO/security fix templates) based on substring matches against an issue's human-readable title, with a generic fallback when nothing matches; explicitly documented as a brittle heuristic pending a real audit-id-keyed lookup.

Small formatting helpers: timeAgo (relative time string from an ISO date), formatDate (long-form date string), and categoryLabel (maps raw issue category ids like 'broken-link' to a human-readable label).

Derives a 1-4 remediation 'phase' for an issue by combining its severity with an inferred effort level (low/medium/high, guessed via regex against the issue title), so the Issue Tracker can order work by real-world priority; also exports PHASES metadata (labels/badges) and shared severity badge/border style maps, and documents the title-matching approach as an intentional interim heuristic.

The app's canonical TypeScript types mirroring the backend's data model: BackendTest and all its nested pieces (issues, screenshots, broken links, console errors, Lighthouse/accessibility/SEO/visual-regression/cross-browser/performance-benchmark results), stats, pipeline, testing policies, branding, team members, monitors, and analytics response shapes, plus the PHASE2_MODULES constant describing optional scan modules.

AI Automation pipeline dashboard: POSTs to /ai-automation/run to fetch the latest completed scan's AI prioritization/root-cause-analysis/fix/CI-CD/release-notes results, auto-refreshes when a new scan completes (polling /tests), and renders the full pipeline (ticket overview, issue analysis, affected component, release notes, CI/CD summary, PR generation with GitHub-connect states, and resolution verification).

Historical analytics screen (sign-in required): fetches api.analytics.get(days) for a selectable 7/30/90-day range and renders summary stat cards plus Recharts visualizations for score trend, top domains, pass/fail trend, and issues-by-severity trend, all computed server-side from real scan history.
Top-level 'Automation' tab container that switches between the Issue Tracker (IssuesPage) and AI Fixes (AIAutomationPage) sub-tabs with an animated tab indicator.

The Dashboard 'Overview' sub-tab: renders the HeroBanner, the latest/active TestPipeline alongside an UnresolvedIssues summary (built by grouping unresolved issues across all tests by category), and the AiTestStudio widget.
Top-level 'Dashboard' tab container switching between Overview (DashboardView), Team (TeamDashboardPage), and Trends (AnalyticsPage) sub-tabs with an animated tab indicator.

Full device-testing lab screen: a searchable/browsable device catalog (favorites, recent, per-OS/brand grouping) feeding a live Playwright session (via useDeviceLabSession) rendered inside DeviceFrame with URL bar, browser-engine/orientation/zoom controls, auto-fit-to-panel sizing, an embeddable DevToolsPanel, and a fullscreen portal mode for an immersive device view.

The Issue Tracker: builds decorated issue rows (phase/effort/host) from all tests, offers phase/site/tab/search filtering, resolves each visible issue's real source file/line via api.locateIssue with bounded concurrency, shows a two-pane feed+ticket-list layout with per-issue 'Go to File' (VS Code deep link) buttons, and a ticket-list export menu (PDF/CSV/Word) via exportReport.ts. Also exports the shared `initials` helper used on the standalone ticket page.

The 'Phase 1' scan-results demo report screen: simulates a live crawl progress counter, renders mock stat cards, Lighthouse gauges, viewport-testing results, broken-link and console-error tables, and sample issue rows, and implements a block-aware PDF export (captures each [data-pdf-block] element separately via html2canvas-pro so cards never get sliced mid-page) that embeds the white-label branding logo/header/footer.

Lists every test that ran at least one Phase 2 module in a left pane (with module-tag chips and live-progress indicators), and shows the selected test's full Phase2ResultsPanel plus a pass/fail launch animation and a PDF/CSV/Word download menu in the right pane.
Reports & Analytics screen combining StatsGrid, ReportsCharts, and ReportsTable, plus a manual 'Export CSV' button that builds and downloads a CSV of all completed tests directly from QADataContext.
Top-level 'Scan Results' tab container switching between Phase 1 (ScanlinePhase1Report), Phase 2 (Phase2ResultsPage), and Device Lab (DeviceLabPage) sub-tabs with an animated tab indicator.

Multi-tab Settings screen: General Profile (read-only account info), Target Domains (real scanned domains plus a session-only manually-tracked list), Continuous Monitoring (create/toggle/run-now/delete scheduled monitors via /api/monitors, polls while open), Custom Testing Policies (CRUD score-range gates via /api/policies), White-label Reports branding form (logo/colors/header/footer via /api/branding), Team management (invite/role-change/remove via /api/team, permission-gated), and a placeholder Integrations tab (Slack/GitHub, not yet backed).

Sign-in-gated team activity screen: fetches team members and shows stat cards (member count, scans this week, contributors), a per-member activity list sorted by scan count, and a recent-activity feed of attributed scans, all derived from QADataContext's tests plus api.team.listMembers.

The Tests tab: combines Header (search + run-new-test), Filters (status/sort), and a paginated TestsTable, computing the filtered/sorted/paginated test list client-side from QADataContext and wiring delete/rerun actions to toast notifications.

Frontend package manifest ('qa-dashboard'): Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript app with dev/build/start/lint scripts; key dependencies include framer-motion, recharts, socket.io-client, @phosphor-icons/react, and jsPDF/jspdf-autotable/docx/jszip/html2canvas-pro for report exports, plus Tailwind CSS v4 as a dev dependency.
Next.js configuration file — currently exports an empty/default NextConfig object with no custom overrides.
TypeScript compiler configuration: ES2017 target, strict mode, bundler module resolution, the Next.js TS plugin, and the `@/*` path alias mapped to `./src/*`.
Flat ESLint config composing eslint-config-next's core-web-vitals and typescript rule sets, overriding the default ignore list to exclude .next/out/build/next-env.d.ts.
PostCSS configuration enabling the @tailwindcss/postcss plugin for Tailwind CSS v4 processing.

Short instruction note for AI coding agents warning that this Next.js version has breaking API/convention/file-structure changes from training data, and to consult node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code.
Single-line file that re-exports/includes AGENTS.md content via an `@AGENTS.md` reference, so Claude-specific tooling picks up the same agent instructions.
